subject.title: Feature request: MEMORY.md size warning/limit enforcement

question: Should `MEMORY.md` budget handling be warning-only in the Control UI first, or should OpenClaw also block saves and provide an archive workflow?
rationale: Current main already covers runtime/doctor diagnostics, while save refusal and auto-archive would change user editing behavior and memory ownership rather than only fixing a missing warning.

options.title: Ship warning-only budget UX
options.body: Expose computed per-file budget state and render yellow/red Control UI and session warnings, leaving save blocking and archive flow for a separate design.

options.title: Enforce save limit now
options.body: Block over-budget `MEMORY.md` saves in the Control UI, accepting that intentional large-memory setups will need an explicit escape hatch or documented override.

options.title: Keep diagnostics only
options.body: Treat `/context`, prompt warnings, and doctor as sufficient and close or narrow the remaining UI feature request.

recommendation.title: Ship warning-only budget UX
recommendation.body: Expose computed per-file budget state and render yellow/red Control UI and session warnings, leaving save blocking and archive flow for a separate design.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current bootstrap truncation warning path and have the clearest feature-history tie to deciding the next UX boundary.
